items.prompt: Is the square f6 light or dark? Check your answer on the board afterwards. This is a self-check: decide from the name before you look.

claims.statement: A pawn on f6 stands on a dark square.

hints: The corner square a1 is dark. Squares next to each other alternate in colour.
Turn the file letter into a number (a=1 ... h=8) and add the rank. Is the sum even or odd?
f is the 6th file and the rank is 6: 6+6=12.
items.explain: a1 is dark and the colours alternate along every rank and file. Add the file number (a=1 to h=8) and the rank number: an even sum is a dark square. For f6 that is 6+6=12, so it is dark.

items.prompt: Is the square h3 light or dark? Check your answer on the board afterwards. This is a self-check: decide from the name before you look.

claims.statement: A pawn on h3 stands on a light square.

hints: The corner square a1 is dark. Squares next to each other alternate in colour.
Turn the file letter into a number (a=1 ... h=8) and add the rank. Is the sum even or odd?
h is the 8th file and the rank is 3: 8+3=11.
items.explain: a1 is dark and the colours alternate along every rank and file. Add the file number (a=1 to h=8) and the rank number: an even sum is a dark square. For h3 that is 8+3=11, so it is light.

items.prompt: A knight stands on c3 and makes five jumps. Does it end on a light or a dark square?

claims.statement: The knight can make five legal jumps from c3, c3-e4-g5-f3-d4-c6 (the black king shuffles between h8 and g8), and then stands on c6.

hints: What colour is c3? Add the file number (c is 3) and the rank number.
A knight changes square colour on every jump. Five jumps is an odd number.
c3 is dark. After an odd number of jumps the knight stands on the other colour.
items.explain: c3 is dark (3+3=6) and a knight changes colour on every jump, so after an odd number of jumps it is on a light square.

items.prompt: A white knight stood on b1 and has been taken off the board. Tap every square it could jump to.

claims.statement: A knight on b1 attacks exactly a3, c3 and d2.
All three squares are legal moves.

hints: A knight jumps two squares along a rank or file and one square sideways.
From b1 there is no room to go down. List the jumps that stay on the board.
Two jumps go up the board; one goes sideways.
items.explain: From b1 the knight reaches a3 and c3 (two ranks up, one file across) and d2 (one rank up, two files across).

items.prompt: A white knight stood on a1 and has been taken off the board. Tap every square where it could stand after exactly two jumps. It may come back to a1.

claims.statement: A knight on a1 attacks exactly b3 and c2.
After the jump to b3 the knight attacks exactly a1, a5, c1, c5, d2, d4.
After the jump to c2 the knight attacks exactly a1, a3, b4, d4, e1, e3.

hints: First list the squares it reaches with one jump from a1. There are only two.
Now jump again from each of those two squares and collect the results.
From b3 it reaches a1, a5, c1, c5, d2 and d4. From c2 it reaches a1, a3, b4, d4, e1 and e3.
items.explain: From a1 the first jump lands on b3 or c2. From b3 the second jump reaches a1, a5, c1, c5, d2, d4; from c2 it reaches a1, a3, b4, d4, e1, e3. Together that makes ten squares, and every one has the same colour as a1.

items.prompt: The white knight on c3 has been taken off the board. Tap every square it could legally move to.

claims.statement: These are all of the knight's legal moves.
The knight also attacks a2, d1 and e4, which hold its own pieces, so it cannot move there.

hints: Start from the eight jumps of a knight on c3. Which ones leave the board?
A knight cannot land on a square held by a piece of its own side.
Look at a2, d1 and e4: whose pieces stand there?
items.explain: A knight on c3 attacks eight squares, but it can only move to those not held by its own pieces. Its own pawns stand on a2 and e4 and its own queen on d1.

items.prompt: A white knight stands on b1. Can it reach e4 in exactly two jumps? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight has exactly these first jumps: a3, c3, d2.
After c3 the knight attacks e4.

hints: List the squares one jump away, then jump again from each.
From c3 a knight reaches e4, among other squares.
b1 to c3 to e4.
items.explain: b1, c3, e4 is a route of two jumps. The colour of e4 matches the colour of b1, as it must after an even number of jumps.

items.prompt: A white knight stands on b1. Can it reach d4 in exactly two jumps? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight has exactly these first jumps: a3, c3, d2.
After the jump to a3 the knight does not attack d4.
After the jump to c3 the knight does not attack d4.
After the jump to d2 the knight does not attack d4.

hints: What colour is b1? What colour is d4?
A knight changes square colour with every jump. After two jumps it is back on the colour it started on.
b1 is light and d4 is dark.
items.explain: A knight changes colour on each jump, so after two jumps it stands on a square of the colour it started on. b1 is light and d4 is dark, so d4 cannot be reached in two jumps.

items.prompt: A white knight stands on b1. Can it reach e4 in exactly two jumps? Predict, then check. (White pawns now stand on a2, b2 and c2.)

claims.statement: The knight has exactly these first jumps: a3, c3, d2.
After c3 the knight attacks e4.

hints: Do the pawns next to the knight stop it from jumping?
A knight jumps over other pieces. It only needs the landing squares to be free of its own pieces.
b1 to c3 to e4 is still open.
items.explain: A knight jumps over the pawns, so they change nothing. The route b1, c3, e4 is still two jumps.

items.prompt: A white knight stands on g1. Can it reach f5 in exactly two jumps (Black does not move)? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight has exactly these first jumps: e2, f3, h3.
After the jump to e2 the knight does not attack f5.
After the jump to f3 the knight does not attack f5.
After the jump to h3 the knight does not attack f5.

hints: List the jumps from g1, then jump again.
What colour is g1, and what colour is f5?
g1 is dark and f5 is light.
items.explain: After two jumps a knight is back on the colour it started on. g1 is dark and f5 is light, so f5 cannot be reached in two jumps.

items.prompt: A white bishop stood on a1 and has been taken off the board. Tap every square of the long diagonal that starts on a1.

claims.statement: A bishop on a1 attacks exactly the seven squares b2 to h8.

hints: On this diagonal the file letter and the rank number go up together.
Start at b2 and add one to the file and one to the rank each step.
b2, c3, d4 and so on up to h8.
items.explain: On the long diagonal from a1 the file and the rank rise together: b2, c3, d4, e5, f6, g7, h8. All seven squares are dark, like a1.

items.prompt: A white bishop stood on h1 and has been taken off the board. Tap every square of the long diagonal that starts on h1.

claims.statement: A bishop on h1 attacks exactly the seven squares g2 to a8.

hints: On this diagonal the file letter goes down while the rank number goes up.
Start at g2 and take one step left and one step up each time.
g2, f3, e4 and so on up to a8.
items.explain: From h1 the file letter goes back one step each time while the rank goes up one: g2, f3, e4, d5, c6, b7, a8. All seven squares are light, like h1.

items.prompt: A black bishop stood on a8 and has been taken off the board. Tap every square it attacked.

claims.statement: A bishop on a8 attacks exactly the seven squares b7 to h1.

hints: A bishop in a corner has only one diagonal.
From a8 the file letter goes up while the rank number goes down.
b7, c6, d5 and so on down to h1.
items.explain: A bishop in the corner has a single diagonal. From a8 the file rises while the rank falls: b7, c6, d5, e4, f3, g2, h1.
